steps.content:
Thought: I can see the data structure. Now I need to:
1. Filter for marine beaches only
2. Filter for years 2002-2023
3. Normalize the "Violation" column (it has "no", "No", "NO", "yes" variants)
4. Find beaches that never had a violation throughout all years

Let me process this:

input.code:
def process(load_all_data) -> pd.DataFrame:
    df = load_all_data.copy()
    
    # Filter marine beaches, years 2002-2023
    df = df[(df['Beach Type Description'] == 'Marine') & (df['Year'] >= 2002) & (df['Year'] <= 2023)]
    
    # Normalize violation column to boolean
    df['is_violation'] = df['Violation'].str.strip().str.lower() == 'yes'
    
    # Find all unique marine beach names
    all_marine_beaches = df['Beach Name'].unique()
    
    # Find beaches that had at least one violation
    violated_beaches = df[df['is_violation']]['Beach Name'].unique()
    
    # Beaches with no violation at all
    safe_beaches = set(all_marine_beaches) - set(violated_beaches)
    
    result = pd.DataFrame({'safe_beach_count': [len(safe_beaches)], 
                           'total_marine_beaches': [len(all_marine_beaches)],
                           'violated_beaches': [len(violated_beaches)]})
    return result
input.summary: Filter marine beaches from 2002-2023, normalize Violation column, find beaches with zero violations across all their data. Returns count of always-safe marine beaches.
